report:
## Window
Round 1, the final round. Span 2026-10-15T21:38 to 2026-10-16T18:33 (+01:00). There were 0 live agents at round time because the solvers had finished. One supervisor (sup-001-r2). This is the post-mortem.

## Succession
4 handoff requests, 3 real handoffs, 2 stubs, 2 kills. handoff_success_rate is 0.6 (n=5). There is no previous window to compare with and no earlier tune to judge. Lineages: L-001 reached gen 2; L-002 and L-003 reached gen 3. Reaching gen 3 in an 8-task run is churn, and both gen-3 lineages are the ones that had a kill.

## Queue and SLOs
Open 0, leased 0, done 8, blocked 0. Verifier: 8 of 8 done, mean score 0.946.
- completions_per_mtok 2.73 (n=8)
- blocked_failed_rate 0 (n=8)
- duplicate_rate 0 (n=7)
- lease_wait_median_s 15.4 (n=8)
- handoff_success_rate 0.6 (n=5)

None has a baseline. Throughput and queue health were fine. Succession is the only weak SLO.

## Actions taken
- One tune: civ_tune handoff_pct 80 → 75, slo handoff_success_rate. It was accepted and expires 19:33. Since the run is over, read it as the recommended seed for the next run, not as a live correction.
- No blockers, alerts or blocked tasks, so I made no replies, reopens or votes.
- No ping. succession_failing needs kills in two consecutive windows, and there is only one window.

## Diagnosis
- **sol-002 (L-002, holding T-008): never_asked, confirmed.** It was never sent a handoff request. One turn took context from under 80% to past kill_pct.
- **sol-003 (L-003, holding T-007): reclassified from no_chance to effectively never_asked / turn-size.** The request did arrive, but context was already at 87%, 7 points past handoff_pct. It was killed 2.72 s later with 0 turns and 0 tool calls, so it never had a turn in which to act.

Raising kill_grace_turns would not have helped: the kill came on context size before any turn happened. Both incidents share one cause: single turns add about 7 or more points of context. That is why the request fires too late or not at all.

T-007 scored 0.9 (missing "michaelmas"). It was the task held across the stub, so a thin stub may explain the lost keyword, but I have not verified that. T-005 scored 0.667 (years_between off by one), which looks like a solver error, not a succession effect.

Changes for the next run:
1. Seed handoff_pct at 75, or lower if per-turn jumps stay around 7 points. Alternatively, widen the gap to kill_pct so one large tool result cannot cross both thresholds.
2. Have the harness send the handoff request before a large tool result is appended, not after the turn.
3. Keep max_attempts, lease_length_s and the board knobs at their seeds. There were no blocks, no duplicates and lease waits were short.
4. Two more verifier checks would help: date arithmetic (T-005) and keyword coverage after a stub (T-007).

## For the operator
The run completed 8 of 8 tasks with a mean score of 0.946 and no blocks. The one systemic weakness is succession: 2 of 5 successions were kills, both caused by large per-turn context growth outruning the 80% handoff threshold. The suggested next-run change is handoff_pct 75 and/or an earlier pre-tool-result check. No ping was sent, because no trigger was met.

Both point to large per-turn context jumps, so the request should land earlier. Final round: this records the recommendation for the next run's seed.
